transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer accounts. My name is Julian. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Julian. I received an email notification yesterday stating that my monthly broadband subscription is increasing by seven pounds and forty pence starting next month, even though I signed an eighteen-month fixed contract.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly review your contract billing terms and available renewal options for you, Tariq. Before we inspect your account records, may I please verify your billing address and your security question answer?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, of course. It is 84 Victoria Park Road, Leicester, LE2 1XD. And the security question answer is my favorite sports team, Leicester City.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Tariq, that confirms your account file. What specific broadband plan is shown on your recent invoice?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is the Full Fibre 300 package. I am a retired university lecturer on a fixed civil service pension, and with energy bills and council tax rising, having an unexpected seven-pound hike thrust upon me has caused me severe financial anxiety!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how concerning unexpected price rises are when you are managing a fixed monthly retirement budget, Tariq. Let us look closely at your agreement and find a tariff that keeps your costs comfortable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Julian, I appreciate your understanding of my situation.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I have understood correctly, you received an annual price adjustment notice reflecting an increase of seven pounds forty on your Full Fibre 300 package, which conflicts with your expectation of a fixed rate across your contract term, and you would like to explore options to reduce that monthly commitment. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. When I signed up last October, the salesperson assured me the price was fixed for eighteen months.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at your original contract schedule, our terms incorporate an annual contractual price adjustment pegged to the Consumer Price Index plus an additional three point nine percent every April.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How can S-Net call it an eighteen-month contract if you can unilaterally increase the price after only six months? That feels completely deceptive to consumers.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The annual inflation adjustment is a standard telecommunications industry provision approved by Ofcom and clearly detailed within paragraph eight point four of our terms.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nobody reads forty pages of fine print when ordering broadband over the phone!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can offer to transition your account to our Full Fibre 150 retention tier immediately at thirty-one pounds a month, which is actually four pounds cheaper than what you pay today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, before we talk about changing tiers, why did the inflation adjustment get calculated at eleven point nine percent total?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The January CPI inflation figure published by the Office for National Statistics was eight percent, and adding three point nine percent yields eleven point nine percent.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It still feels completely unreasonable for loyal customers who pay on time every month.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you had bothered to read section 8.4 of your contract agreement, you wouldn't need to ask me why prices rise every single April.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is no need to be rude and condescending! I asked a reasonable question about my hard-earned money. Please maintain a professional tone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize for my phrasing, Tariq. Let us look at the financial options available on your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. Now tell me more about this Full Fibre 150 tier.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Full Fibre 150 tier delivers download speeds of one hundred and fifty megabits per second and upload speeds of thirty megabits per second on a new eighteen-month agreement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will 150 megabits be fast enough for high definition streaming and video calling?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, 150 megabits effortlessly supports multiple simultaneous 4K streams and uninterrupted video calls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And the price would be fixed at thirty-one pounds?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It would be thirty-one pounds per month, subject to the standard April CPI plus three point nine percent clause in future years.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: At least thirty-one pounds lowers my current monthly outgoings by four pounds immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It generates an instant annual saving of forty-eight pounds across the first year.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That definitely helps with my monthly budgeting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you also wish to keep your inclusive weekend landline calls package on the contract?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my wife uses the landline on Sunday afternoons to speak with her sister in Edinburgh.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can bundle the Weekend Calls feature at zero additional cost as part of this loyalty discount package.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that is very generous, thank you Julian.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will apply the customer retention credit code RET-31-LOYALTY to lock in that thirty-one pound monthly tariff.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does this require any new equipment or an engineer visit to our property?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No engineer visit is needed because your optical ONT unit and S-Net Hub 5 remain completely identical; the speed provisioning updates electronically at midnight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is very seamless. Will I receive a revised contract summary by email?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, our automated system has just sent a pre-contract information sheet and contract summary to your registered email address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking my iPad inbox... yes, the S-Net contract confirmation email has arrived showing thirty-one pounds per month including weekend calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please click the digital acknowledgment link inside that email to confirm your acceptance of the revised eighteen-month term.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking the green Accept and Confirm button now... the webpage says 'Thank you, your new contract terms are now confirmed'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to check on your current broadband service, Tariq, is your internet connection and WiFi performing normally across all rooms today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the physical fiber connection and WiFi have been working very reliably throughout the house.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check your paperless billing preferences to ensure invoice notifications continue arriving by email rather than paper surcharge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I prefer email notifications because paper bills cost an extra three pounds per month on the statement.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Paperless billing is fully active on your profile, so no paper fee will ever be applied.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is very good to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under the UK Direct Debit Guarantee scheme, your payment date remains locked on the first of each month, protected by your bank.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Having the payment leave on the first aligns perfectly with my civil service pension deposit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented the retention package transition and rate adjustment on your account file.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for getting the price reduced, Julian.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your next monthly direct debit will reflect the thirty-one pound amount.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me much greater peace of mind with my monthly budget.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your S-Net contract or broadband services that I can assist you with today, Tariq?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that resolves my billing concern completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may receive a brief customer satisfaction survey by SMS after this call; we would appreciate any feedback on your experience today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will complete the survey. Good afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Tariq. Have a pleasant afternoon and take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, goodbye.
